title: Network requests and response inspection
learningObjectives: Explain network requests and response inspection and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: The Network panel records requests and responses, including URL, method, status, headers, payload, timing, and transferred resources. It can help identify failed API calls, caching behaviour, redirects, and slow resources.
understand.whyItMatters: A page may look broken because a request failed or returned unexpected data. Inspect the actual response rather than guessing from the UI alone.
understand.analogy: The Network panel is a delivery log showing each request sent and each response received.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The snippet prints status and content type for a request; the Network panel exposes the full exchange and timing.

examples.explanation: The snippet prints status and content type for a request; the Network panel exposes the full exchange and timing.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect a lesson JSON request. Record its status, content type, cache behaviour, and response body.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.
